name: Ballari (incl. Vijayanagara)
headline: A tracking drive found 259 out-of-school children but brought back only 38.
summary: In a drive reported in January 2025, officials identified 259 out-of-school children in Ballari but brought only 38 back to school. The deep-research report's claims about mining, poverty and mass weddings rested on a social-media post and a statewide article that does not name Ballari, so they are not used here.

reasons.detail: A tracking drive identified 259 out-of-school children but managed to bring only 38 back to class.

In 2020 a Ballari child rights commission member said most schools in the district only ran classes 6-8 and higher classes were elsewhere, away from hostels; girls dropped out and parents hesitated over distance.

Ballari had 395 vacancies among 1,014 sanctioned government high school posts in 2025, worst in Siruguppa (157 of 269) and Sandur (92 of 181); guest teachers covered 434 posts, with maths and science gaps.

Ballari ranked 29th in 2025 with 60 government high schools below 40% pass; in June 2024 the CM sought suspension of Vijayanagara's education officers after its education ranking fell from 10th to 27th.

State-level 2018-19 survey, where Ballari recorded 5,132 out-of-school children, cited migration, disinterest, domestic work, distance and parental reluctance to educate girls. Not broken out for Ballari.

entries.factor: % Population Living in Households with Improved Sanitation
entries.why: Ballari (including Vijayanagara) has many rural areas with poor sanitation. Lack of toilets in schools can force menstruating girls to miss classes and drop out.
entries.mechanism: No toilets at school -> girls skip school monthly -> attendance drops -> exit from school

proof.claim: Millions of Indian girls drop out annually due to menstruation issues
proof.quote: Millions of adolescent girls drop out of school every year

dominantFactorWhy.gaps: Local information on sanitation facilities and medium of instruction in Ballari and Vijayanagara taluk was unavailable, so we rely on general findings.

changes.summary: Villagers at Kolur, Ballari district protested for toilets and drinking water at their government school (2025); officials promised toilet repairs within 15 days. A 2026 complaint flags unhygienic washrooms at a Hosapete school.

findings.claim: Villagers in Kolur, Ballari district demanded a permanent building, toilets and clean water for the government higher primary school; officials promised to repair existing toilets within 15 days.
findings.quote: The protesters submitted a memorandum urging the authorities to construct a permanent school building on the available government land and provide essential facilities such as toilets and clean drinking water.

findings.claim: A complaint on the Namma Shaale platform flags unhygienic washrooms at GMHPS Mariyammana Halli in Hosapete needing cleaning, repairs and running water.
findings.quote: At GMHPS Mariyammana Halli in Hosapete, Ballari, a complaint highlights unhygienic washrooms that require cleaning, repairs, running water and regular maintenance.

changes.summary: No district-specific source found for Ballari or Vijayanagara; only a region-wide report mentioning missing libraries in many Kalyana Karnataka government schools.

findings.claim: Across Kalyana Karnataka, many government schools are reported to have poor infrastructure, including a lack of libraries, classrooms, toilets and drinking water; a region-wide statement.
findings.quote: Apart from the shortage of teachers, many govt schools also have poor infrastructure, including inadequate drinking water, toilet facilities, electricity, lack of classrooms, libraries, playgrounds and compound walls.

changes.summary: Ballari district reports show a crumbling school at Yattinabudihal with classes held outdoors (2025) and a roof collapse at Sirawar school with 9 of 19 rooms old. A regional claim cites 18,022 classrooms needing repair.

findings.claim: At Yattinabudihal government school in Ballari district a crumbling wall left classes being held in the open; parents say more than 80 students crowd one usable classroom.
findings.quote: The crumbling wall of Yattinabudihal Government School in Ballari district has resulted in classes being held out in the open.

findings.claim: A roof layer fell in a deteriorated room at the Sirawar government higher primary school in Ballari taluk, seriously injuring a student; 9 of its 19 rooms are old.
findings.quote: The school has 19 rooms, of which 9 are old, and a student sustained a serious head injury when the layer of the roof of a deteriorated room fell.

findings.claim: Opposition leader R Ashoka, citing a Kannada media report, claimed 18,022 classrooms in Kalyana Karnataka need repair, 8,006 of them declared dilapidated; a regional, partisan claim.
